# globmatch — module contract (authoritative)

`globmatch.py` at the worktree root: `matches(pattern, name) -> bool` — POSIX-style glob
matching of a whole name.

## Grammar (the ONLY metacharacters)

- `*` — zero or more characters, **none of which may be `/`**.
- `?` — exactly one character, which may not be `/`.
- `[...]` — one character from the set; `[!...]` matches one character **not** in the set.
  Inside a set, `-` denotes a range (`[a-z]`) and `\` escapes the next character. A `]`
  ends the set; to match a literal `]`, escape it. An unterminated `[` makes the pattern
  **invalid**.
- `\` — escapes the next character literally (e.g. `\*` matches a literal `*`). A trailing
  lone `\` makes the pattern **invalid**.
- Any other character matches itself literally.

## Matching semantics

- A match must cover the **whole** `name` (anchored at both ends).
- There is no `**`: `*` simply does not cross `/`.
- An invalid pattern raises `ValueError`. A non-`str` `pattern` or `name` raises
  `TypeError`.

## General

Standard library only. This document is the authoritative statement of the module's
behavior.
